newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish-German leasing firm PLP targets machinery.
newsitem.headline: Polish-German leasing firm PLP targets machinery.

text.p: Polski Leasing Przemyslowy SA (PLP), a new venture between Deutsche Leasing AG and Bank Pekao SA, plans to secure 10 percent of Poland's industrial machinery leasing market, the German firm's president said on Thursday.

"The creation of a joint venture means using the experience of Grupa Pekao SA, linked with the the know-how of a leasing firm which has operated for a long time on the international arena," Deutsche Leasing's Horst Figge told a news conference. @
PLP, which began operations in May with initial capital of four million zlotys, is a 50-50 venture between Deutsche Leasing and Poland's Bank Pekao SA group, seen privatised next year.
Figge said PLP would focus mainly on leasing industrial machinery but would also concentrate on the leasing of means of transport and computer equipment.
In 1996 the value of leased goods in Poland totalled $2.48 billion, showing growth of 97 percent over the previous year, according to figures from the Conference of Leasing Companies. @
"The Polish market still has enormous development potential when it comes to leasing," said Figge.
He said financial investment in leasing in 1996 amounted to 7.2 percent of overall investments in Poland, compared with 18 percent in Germany.
Deutsche Leasing operates in Germany, the Czech Republic, France, Italy and Hungary. In 1996 it leased goods worth 2.84 billion German marks. @
State-owned commercial bank Pekao SA heads a group also comprising state-owned commercial Pomorski Bank Kredytowy SA, Powszechny Bank Gospodarczy SA and Bank Depozytowo-Kredytowy SA.
